To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
heparan sulfate chains are initiated by xylose-2-phosphorylserine and that this linkage region is identical with that of chondroitin sulfate.
heparan sulfate chains have a 2-galactosyllinkage region, that the xylose residue in this region is phosphorylated and that the phosphate ester is located to C- 2 of xylose.
the structure of the heparin/heparan sulfate-proteoglycan linkage region is Galbeta 1-4GlcNAc-beta 1-4Galbeta 1-3Galbeta 1-O-Ser(2-0-P-Xyl).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of heparan sulfates.
the elucidation of the structure of the heparin linkage region.
the structure of heparan sulfates and the mechanism of biosynthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heparan sulfate chains are linked to serine residues of proteins via the following sequence of sugars: galactose-galactose-xylose-xylose-phosphate.
the heparan sulfates of bovine lung are linked to protein via a 2-galactose/1-phosphoxylose/1-serine structure.
heparan sulfate is linked to the protein core via a linkage region consisting of 2 galactosyl, 1 xylosyl and 1 serinyl residue, and that the xylosyl residue bears a 2-phosphoester.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linkage region of heparan sulfates has the structure Galbeta1-4Glcbeta1-3(2-PhO)Xylbeta1-4Ser.
the linkage region of heparan and chondroitin sulfates is structurally identical.
the heparan sulfates are initiated by the same mechanism as the proteochondroitins and that the linkage region is identical to that of the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heparan-sulfate linkage region is a trisaccharidic sequence of the type galactosyl-(1-4)-galactosyl-(l-3)-2-phosphoxylosyl-serine.
the heparan-sulfate-protein linkage region has the structure Galbeta1-3Galbeta1-4Xyl-2-PO4.
the heparan sulfates of bovine lung contain the sequence Gal-Gal-Xyl-2-P.
